spans.s:
dvi, form of dva in composition and derivation.
[475^6.]

dvi-já, a. twice-born; as m. member of
one of the three upper castes, re-born by
virtue of investiture (see √nī + upa), 60^2,
58^20, 59^4, 62^7; in a narrower sense, a Brahman,
 21^14, 43^4, 55^9, 64^16.

dvi-jánman, a. having double birth; as
m. same as dvija; man of one of the three
upper castes, 59^1. [acct, 1300c.]

dvijottama, m. the highest of the twiceborn,
 i. e. a Brahman. [dvija + uttama.]
dvitā́, adv. just so; so also; equally.
dvídhā, adv. in two parts, in twain. [1104.]

dvi-pád [391], a. having two feet; as m.
the two-footed one, man, 16^2; as n. sing.
that which is two-footed, collectively, men,
901, 3, 92^3. [cf. δίποδα, Lat. bipedem, ‘biped.
’]

dvi-pada, f. -ī, a. having (taken) two
steps.

dvi-pravrājin, f. -nī, a. in f. going
after two (men), unchaste, 98^14.

√dviṣ (dvéṣṭi, dviṣṭé; didvéṣa; ádvikṣat,
-ata; dviṣṭá; dvéṣṭum). hate; show
hatred; be hostile. [cf. ὀ-δύσ-αντο, ‘became
wroth,’ w. prothetic ο.]

dvíṣ, vbl. hating, in cpds; as f. hate; as m.
concrete, hater, foe. [√dviṣ.]

dvís, adv. twice. [see dvi, dva: cf. δίς,
Lat. bis, *dvis, ‘twice’: the radically cognate
Eng. twice is a gen. form.]

dvīpín, a. having islands or island-like
spots; as m. leopard; tiger. [dvīpa.]
